sovereign_country.strategic_role: 苏伊士运河经济特区、辐射中东及北非的低成本轻工制造

business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Air Freight Forwarding and Cargo Aircraft Charter

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law with Islamic Sharia as a source of legislation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agadir Free Trade Agreement (Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, Tunisia)
Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) Treaty

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended (with Executive Regulations by the Central Bank of Egypt); Law No. 159 of 1981 on Commercial Companies; Law No. 72 of 2017 on Investment; Executive Regulations of the Investment Law (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2310 of 2017) requiring identification and disclosure of ultimate beneficial owners to the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) and the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Passport / Valid Travel Document of all natural person UBOs and managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Passport Authority in the country of origin / relevant foreign authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where the country is an Apostille contracting party; Egypt has been an Apostille party since entry into force of the Convention in Egypt, June 14, 2022); otherwise Consular Legalization by the Egyptian Consulate in the issuing country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Corporate Existence for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or Chamber of Commerce in the corporate shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as above

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing the local incorporation agent and managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate governing body (Board of Directors) or notary of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as above

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter / Source of Funds and Source of Wealth declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank (licensed in the country of origin) and signing party
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as above

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior officers against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and consolidated lists, EU and UK sanctions lists, and the Egyptian domestic terrorism and money laundering blacklist maintained by the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) and the FRA. Enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons (PEPs) in accordance with CBE regulations under Law No. 80 of 2002; family members and close associates are included. Screening must be documented contemporaneously and retained for at least 5 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Investment Services Online Platform (www.gafi.gov.eg); pre-incorporation name reservation via the GAFI one-stop shop and the Egyptian Commercial Registry (Ministry of Trade and Industry).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Every company name must be in Arabic, optionally accompanied by a foreign language transliteration. The Arabic name must be written in Arabic characters, must not clash with proper grammatical script or Arabic-Islamic phraseology, and must not include foreign words unless they are in common usage or consist of the Arabic transliteration of the founder's name. The foreign transliteration may not conflict with Arabic translation or cause phonetic confusion with an existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within the name reservation process, if the proposed name is rejected, the applicant or its legal representative may file a written administrative appeal with the Name Clearance Committee at GAFI within 15 working days from the date of rejection notification. The appeal should state the grounds for the chosen name, include evidence of prior existing registrations or the functional necessity of the name, and may be supported by the Egyptian trademark registry if the name is used as a trade mark. GAFI is required to issue a reasoned decision within 30 working days. A further appeal may be filed with the First Instance Administrative Court of the State Council if the administrative appeal is denied. The reservation window of 30 days may not be extended unless an appeal is pending, in which case the reservation is held in abeyance with a pending appeal status.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not accepted as an exclusive statutory registered office in Egypt for an air cargo charter broker, because the law requires a physical, identifiable address in Egypt that can receive official notices and be inspected by the authorities. A physical lease agreement (signed, notarized, and registered with the local real estate registry) is mandatory. A virtual office may be used only as an additional business-correspondence address, but cannot serve as the registered office for GAFI, the Commercial Registry, or the Civil Aviation Authority licensing purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 30% annually. GAFI or the Ministry of Civil Aviation/licensing authority may conduct unannounced on-site verification during the pre-licensing phase, and annually thereafter, given the air cargo classification and the transport/regulatory sensitivity of the industry. The presence of sub-leases or remote management arrangements increases inspection likelihood.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GAFI company name reservation and certificate fee (non-refundable)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff prescribed in the GAFI fee schedule (EGP equivalent converted to USD based on prevailing exchange rate)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Registry pre-registration clearance and UBO statement filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial Registry / General Authority for Investment and Free Zones
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory government fee schedule for preparation and filing of the UBO statement and commercial form (estimated from Ministerial Decrees of the Ministry of Trade and Industry)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial certification and legal translation of Arabic incorporation documents (including apostille coordination)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Public Notary / certified legal translation office / Ministry of Foreign Affairs or designated apostille authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for notarial acts and official translation fees; apostille fee per document as fixed by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified English and Arabic legal opinion on UBO/AML clearance (drafted by retained Egyptian counsel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market hourly/flat-fee benchmark for corporate due diligence and AML clearance opinions (US$ 600–1,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GAFI pre-incorporation document vetting and e-registration facilitation service legal fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Retained law firm / GAFI one-stop-shop facilitator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for professional administrative clearance coordination

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office lease deposit (first installment + notarization) for required physical premises
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Lessor / notary / Ministry of Finance real estate stamp duties
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for small commercial office lease deposit in Cairo or Alexandria; not a government statutory tariff but a market-floor requirement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and legalization handling for foreign-issued due diligence documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Apostille competent authority in the issuing foreign country or Egyptian Consulate in the issuing country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government fixed per-document fee as published by the apostille/consulate (estimated aggregated fee for 4 documents)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA / Maslahat Al-Dara'eb) - Unified E-Tax Services Portal: https://tax.gov.eg; e-invoicing clearance portal: https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg; official issuer of the unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) covering income tax, VAT, and stamp duty.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing an EG LLC must: (1) appoint a local tax representative under Article 12 of Income Tax Law 91/2005 with a notarized power of attorney; (2) obtain commercial registration with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) or the Ministry of Trade Commercial Registry; (3) obtain the entity's unified national ID number; (4) file the unified tax registration application on the E-Tax Portal (https://tax.gov.eg), attaching the commercial registry extract, certificate of incorporation, LLC contract, board resolution appointing the tax agent, beneficial-ownership declarations, and evidence of the licensed air cargo brokerage activity; (5) upon ETA issuance of the TIN, complete VAT registration under Law 67/2016 when projected annual taxable turnover meets or exceeds EGP 500,000; and (6) procure an ETA-approved digital signature certificate and API credentials for the mandatory B2B e-invoicing clearance system before issuing any invoice.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch pass-through election exists under Egyptian law; an LLC is mandatorily treated as a taxable person under Income Tax Law 91/2005 as amended by Law 30/2023. Available statutory elections: (i) VAT group election for related Egyptian taxable persons under Article 16 of VAT Law 67/2016; (ii) fiscal-year alignment election subject to ETA approval; (iii) transfer-pricing Advance Pricing Agreement application under Law 30/2023; (iv) loss carryforward election limited to a maximum of five years with no carryback; and (v) foreign-currency export-account arrangements under Central Bank of Egypt circulars supporting the 180-day FX repatriation window for zero-rated export brokerage.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Value-Added Tax under Law 67/2016, administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority; supplemented by stamp duty and selective excise taxes where applicable
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual value of taxable supplies of goods and services during the preceding 12 months; VAT registration application is mandatory within 60 days of crossing the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory Egypt Business E-Invoicing System (EBECS) with ETA real-time clearance. Every B2B invoice issued by the air cargo charter brokerage must be transmitted via ETA-approved SOAP/REST APIs before or at issuance, validated in real time, and stamped with an ETA-issued UUID and QR code using a qualified digital signature. Invoices failing ETA clearance are legally non-compliant and the buyer loses input VAT deduction. B2C e-receipts are separately phased in under the ERGS mandate; export-related invoices require additional electronic linkage to customs export declarations where goods are involved.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Article 9 of VAT Law 67/2016 for: (i) goods physically exported from Egypt; (ii) services rendered wholly to non-residents and consumed entirely outside Egypt; (iii) international transport of goods and passengers; and (iv) ancillary air freight services directly linked to international carriage. For an air cargo charter broker, commission and charter fees invoiced to a non-resident principal for international cargo carriage qualify for the 0% rate where the service is not performed for use within Egypt; domestic inland haulage and services consumed in Egypt remain taxable at 14%. Full substantiation of physical export, non-resident status, and actual repatriation of hard-currency proceeds into the Egyptian banking system is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document - SAD)
Commercial invoice (ETA-cleared e-invoice containing UUID and QR code)
Master Air Waybill / House Air Waybill evidencing international carriage
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice issued by an authorized Egyptian bank evidencing receipt of the full foreign-currency proceeds
Executed cargo charter or brokerage agreement identifying the non-resident principal
ETA zero-rating substantiation file including booking confirmations, load sheets, and proof of cargo crossing the Egyptian border
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA export-audit discipline requires proof of physical export, non-resident counterparty status, and full FX repatriation within applicable CBE-prescribed timelines, with 180 days as the governing window in this dossier. Failure to substantiate triggers reversal of zero-rating, re-taxation at the 14% standard VAT rate, monthly default interest of 1.5% under Article 27 of VAT Law 67/2016, administrative fines of up to EGP 25,000, and criminal evasion sanctions including imprisonment and fines calculated as multiples of the tax evaded under Law 30/2023 for fraudulent documentation, forged air waybills, or falsified inward remittance certificates. VAT refund claims are suspended during inspection and the appointed tax agent's license may be revoked for facilitating abusive export claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a managed floating exchange rate regime under Central Bank of Egypt oversight. Capital account convertibility remains restricted for residents, requiring prior CBE approval for profit remittances and capital repatriation exceeding thresholds. Non-residents benefit from greater flexibility for FDI inflows. Profit remittance hurdles include mandatory tax clearance, source-of-funds verification, and CBE notification for amounts above EGP 100,000.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from air cargo charter services must be surrendered to authorized banks within 90 days of collection. Surrender is mandatory at the prevailing market rate or official rate per CBE directives. Non-compliance triggers penalties, including fines up to 10% of the amount and potential license suspension.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility rating. Offshore digital EMIs are prohibited for Egyptian residents under CBE FX controls; all cross-border activity must route through licensed local banks with full KYC/AML compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors and authorized signatories is mandatory for KYC interviews and account opening. Remote corporate onboarding is not permitted under current CBE guidelines for entities with foreign ownership or elevated risk profiles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or shell company indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner declaration, corporate structure chart, and notarized ownership documents

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions inconsistent with declared business activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Air cargo charter contracts, flight manifests, insurance policies, and regulatory approvals from Egyptian aviation authorities

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections routed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION'. Verification includes board resolutions, valuation reports, and CBE notification for amounts exceeding EGP 100,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements settled through SWIFT MT103 or MT202. Commercial LCs issued under UCP 600. Purpose codes must specify trade nature (e.g., 'GOODS PURCHASE' for cargo-related). All FX conversions reported to CBE.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Corporate Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year; calendar-year taxpayers due on or before 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 2% per month on unimposed tax; late-filing fixed penalty under Tax Procedures Law; enforced collection through treasury garnishment; criminal prosecution for deliberate non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements and Tax Reconciliation Package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) One-Stop Shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed simultaneously with the corporate income tax return; in all cases no later than 6 months after the annual general meeting approving the statements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete tax return treatment; disallowance of deductions; late filing penalties; after repeated non-submission GAFI may initiate company compulsory winding-up.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO and Shareholding Register Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Corporate Registry and the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (through the one-stop shop)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year and always before the ordinary general meeting; any movement of 25% or more of ownership must be confirmed within 30 days of the transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine under the Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Law; possible suspension of the commercial registration and revocation of the forwarding licence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registration Renewal and Company Data Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office attached to GAFI / Ministry of Interior
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On the anniversary date of the commercial registration; filings must be completed by no later than 31 December of each calendar year for calendar-year companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Cumulative late fees under the Commercial Registry Law; a persistent lapse of more than 60 days may trigger administrative strike-off of the registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Air Cargo Charter Broker Annual Operating Licence Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Civil Aviation Authority (ECAA) - Economic Licensing and Air Transport Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal application must be lodged no later than 30 days before the expiry of the one-year operating licence, which runs from the date of the original grant.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate grounding of charter brokerage operations; licence cancellation and removal from the approved cargo agent list; separate administrative fine under Civil Aviation Law.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is mandatory for: (i) all joint-stock companies; (ii) LLCs meeting the medium/large enterprise test under Companies Law 180/2018, generally annual revenue above EGP 10,000,000, total assets above EGP 20,000,000, or 25 or more employees; and (iii) any licensed entity in the air-freight forwarding and aircraft charter broking sector, regardless of size, as required by the ECAA licence conditions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), closely aligned with IFRS as issued by the Egyptian Ministry of Finance; full IFRS permitted for cross-border listed or internationally financed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must confirm to GAFI, by way of the annual corporate return, the complete chain of individuals exercising direct or indirect ownership or control. A separate UBO confirmation is required for each shareholder structure change during the year, including but not limited to any transfer of quotas. The confirmation must be reflected in the statutory Register of Members before the ordinary general meeting is convened; failure to maintain the register invalidates the annual confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of General Meetings and Board Meeting Minutes
Register of Pledges and Encumbrances on LLC Quotas

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% on taxable corporate income under Egyptian Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, as amended.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic broad CIT holiday for LLCs. Investors licensed under Investment Law No. 72/2017 may be eligible for an incentive package including accelerated depreciation, investment cost deductions of 20% to 50%, and project-specific loss of up to 10 years; export-oriented air freight logistics projects located in Suez Canal Economic Zone or designated industrial zones may qualify for reduced taxable income treatment if annual export proceeds exceed 50% of total revenue. No standalone permanent tax holiday is available for the air cargo charter broker business.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 12 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and the annual Transfer Pricing Disclosure Form, filed via the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-Tax electronic filing portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg. The TP disclosure and supporting financial statements, in Arabic or with certified Arabic translation, must be filed together with Form 12.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing of Form 12, covering a 12-month taxable year; quarterly provisional income tax instalments based on prior tax liability are generally required during the year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form 12 must be submitted within four months after the end of the taxable year (for a calendar-year LLC, by no later than 30 April of the following year). Extensions are not statutorily automatic and require an application accepted by the ETA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial registration number, tax card number, legal form, registered address, and fiscal year dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident foreign company that has created a permanent establishment (PE) in Egypt must enter the branch registration number and the tax card issued for the PE. If no PE exists but the foreign company has Egyptian-source trading income, a TP-only disclosure may be required without Form 12.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from air cargo charter brokerage: commissions, brokerage fees, overrides, handling fees and other invoiced service revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only revenue attributable to the Egyptian PE and Egyptian-source activity is reportable. Commissions earned by negotiation performed wholly outside Egypt are excluded only when supported by contracts, emails and evidence of decision-making; treaty dependence on an Egyptian PE must be avoided.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income, foreign exchange gains, interest income and realized gains on disposal of fixed assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include Egypt-source interest or bank deposit income; foreign exchange gains from the PE's Egyptian accounts must be included. Treaty capital-gain exemptions do not apply unless the relevant DTA article and TRC are supplied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: aircraft positioning and handling costs, subcontracted charter capacity, crew and staff compensation, social insurance, insurance premiums, communication, legal and licensing fees and freight management systems.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are limited to expenses wholly and exclusively incurred for the Egyptian PE. Payments to related foreign parties must satisfy the arm's length rule; head-office general administrative cost allocations are deductible only to the extent documented and attributable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfers of losses from prior years, limited to five years, and loss utilisation computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE cannot carry forward losses incurred before the PE registration year; losses of a foreign head office cannot be transferred to the Egyptian PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation, applicable CIT rate, tax credits and final tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must compute branch-level taxable profit as if it were a separate entity; treaty relief reduces Egypt-source income only after ETA recognition, and any foreign tax credit is applied in the residence state, not in Egypt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all related-party transactions, counterparty jurisdiction, transaction value, transfer pricing method applied, and contemporaneous documentation references.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with related-party transactions exceeding the statutory threshold must file the TP disclosure with the annual return; a foreign intermediary lacking an Egyptian PE must nonetheless file the disclosure if Egyptian-source transactions are carried out through an Egyptian agent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a monthly late-payment surcharge of 2% of the unpaid tax for each month or fraction of a month, capped at 50% of the tax due, plus an administrative penalty of up to EGP 10,000 for failure to submit the return by the statutory deadline. Material understatement or exclusion of income may attract a penalty of 30% to 40% of the understated tax; persistent non-compliance may lead to criminal prosecution of the responsible directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends paid by an Egyptian LLC to non-resident shareholders. The rate is a final withholding for the non-resident, and no further PE tax is imposed on the dividend distribution as separate corporate income tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Egyptian paying entity must withhold at the statutory 10% unless the non-resident beneficial owner provides a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence-state tax authority for the relevant fiscal year. The applicant must also submit a completed DTA relief questionnaire or treaty application to the ETA, evidence of beneficial ownership, and — where a reduced dividend rate requires shareholding — proof of continuous holding of the relevant ownership percentage. ETA approval may be granted before payment by way of reduced withholding or after payment as a refund claim; claims are time-barred if not brought within the treaty limitation period (commonly three to five years).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT: 10% on interest paid to non-resident lenders and 20% on royalties and technical service fees where the foreign owner is not taxable through a PE. Under Egypt's DTA network, interest is commonly reduced to 10% and royalties to 10% or 12%, subject to the specific treaty, the TRC, and the absence of an Egyptian PE or agent acting for the foreign recipient.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10,000,000 in aggregate related-party transaction value per fiscal year triggers mandatory Local File documentation; a Master File is expected when the multinational group's consolidated Egyptian-taxed revenue or the intercompany transactions involving Egypt exceed EGP 120,000,000, subject to the provisions of the Egyptian Transfer Pricing Guidelines.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply a separate Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the ETA applies substance-over-form, business-purpose and general anti-abuse rules under the Income Tax Law No. 91/2005. A shell LLC that merely arranges air cargo charters on paper, without employees, physical office, active negotiation, invoicing, supervision of shipments or risk exposure, will be re-characterised as a conduit. The PE may be deemed present, DTA benefits denied, and the underlying charter income re-allocated to the beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of brokerage commissions and charter fees received from foreign carriers, use of dual invoicing, depositing receipts into private foreign accounts without declaring Egypt-source revenue, or manufacturing fictional deductions for charter operating costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of two to five years under Law No. 91/2005 and a fine equal to twice the tax evaded subject to a minimum of EGP 20,000; confiscation of bank balances and assets representing undeclared commissions; administrative penalties of 30% to 40% of the understatement plus a monthly late-payment surcharge of 2% until full payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, managers and de facto signatories who knowingly file false Form 12 are jointly and severally liable, may face personal attachment against their assets, travel bans, seizure of passports, civil restitution to the tax authority and imprisonment for the period provided for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance / Erosion of Egypt Taxable Base
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying non-arm's length high commissions to a foreign affiliate broker, failing to submit the annual TP Disclosure Form, absence of contemporaneous TP study, entering into back-to-back charter contracts with a related airline at artificial rates, or shifting Egypt booking income to a tax-haven entity without staff or functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA re-determination of taxable income at arm's length, with a TP adjustment; disallowance of the excessive portion of the payment; statutory late-payment interest of 2% per month on the additional tax; a separate penalty of up to 1% of the value of undisclosed related-party transactions or EGP 100,000, whichever applies, and a five-year statute of limitations reopening closed years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or implement aggressive transfer pricing without supporting analysis are liable in restitution for the unpaid tax where the company becomes insolvent; the court may issue personal or travel restrictions pending settlement, and criminal charges are possible when the TP failure is linked to false documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Zero Economic Substance / Sham Broker
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC is registered in Egypt only to obtain a tax ID and bank account while all negotiation, contracting, billing and risk-management functions are performed by the foreign parent, with no qualified employees in Egypt, no physical premises, no Egyptian-origin invoices and no evidence of commercially meaningful activity beyond commission pass-through.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA may disregard the entity under the general anti-abuse rule, attribute the taxable profit to the foreign principal and charge 22.5% CIT plus branch-profit remittance tax and WHT on deemed distributed income; the Commercial Registry may cancel the license for misrepresenting the head office; the imposing penalty may include 2% monthly delay surcharge and fines of up to EGP 100,000 for non-resident registration violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee and de facto directors face piercing of the corporate veil, personal liability for the unpaid taxes, civil liability to creditors misled by the sham, confiscation of commissions, travel bans and exclusion from the commercial register; criminal liability for fraud may attach where false declarations are used.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering / Sanctions Evasion / Trade-Based Money Laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Swift Wire / Fedwire payments from sanctioned air carriers or ultimate beneficial owners, conducting cargo charter finance operations through undisclosed intermediary accounts, splitting large cash payments, incomplete customer due diligence, falsely invoicing high-value cargo charters, or failing to report suspicious transactions under Law No. 80/2002.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to seven years and confiscation of the proceeds derived from money laundering; fine equal to twice the amount involved or an EGP 1,000,000 minimum for repeat offenders; revocation of the cargo agency license, removal from the official Civil Aviation economic operator list, freezing of assets and prohibition against participation in public procurement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers and substantial shareholders who knew or willfully ignored the source of funds are personally subject to criminal penalties, asset forfeiture, compensation orders, travel bans, and disqualification from acting as a director or compliance officer; personal liability extends to unpaid AML fines and costs.
